facts.claim: The experimental group showed a decrease in functional coupling between the hippocampus and associated brain regions after three months of using GPS navigation in AR glasses, while the control group showed an increase.
facts.quote: the experimental group showed FC decrease after three months of using GPS navigation implemented in AR glasses in contrast to FC increase in the control group without such intervention.

facts.claim: No effect of using GPS navigation in AR glasses was observed on navigational abilities.
facts.quote: Importantly, no effect of intervention on navigational abilities was observed.

facts.claim: No significant differences emerged between experts and novices, nor females and males, for the retrieval of spatial information presented on 2D maps with a simple design and content.
facts.quote: no significant differences emerged between neither experts and novices, nor females and males for the retrieval of spatial information presented on 2D maps with a simple design and content.

facts.claim: Analysis shows that paths tend to be drawn more frequently at first but soon decrease in frequency in favour of landmarks.
facts.quote: Analysis shows that paths tend to be drawn more frequently at first but soon decrease in frequency in favour of landmarks.

facts.claim: Nodes, boundaries, and districts tend to be drawn throughout the drawing process but are much less frequent.
facts.quote: Nodes, boundaries, and districts tend to be drawn throughout the drawing process but are much less frequent.

research.angle: While externalizing navigation to GPS technology is linked to a decrease in hippocampal functional connectivity, it does not appear to affect actual navigational abilities.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that technology-assisted navigation is associated with measurable changes in brain connectivity but does not currently show a measurable degradation in spatial navigation skills.
research.caveat: The study on hippocampal connectivity was limited to a three-month period and did not observe any impact on actual cognitive navigational abilities.
